record.paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
record.original_question: Let f (z) be analytic and bounded for ℜzP> 0. Suppose that |α| < 12 π and that (rn ) is a sequence of positive integers with rn = ∞. Show that the exponential type of f on the sequence zn = rn eiα is equal to the type of f on the ray z = reiα . (Proofs by Boas [102] and by Levinson [516] for α = 0 do not seem to work for |α| > 14 π.) (J. Korevaar)

evidence.quote: Let f (z) be analytic and bounded for ℜzP> 0. Suppose that |α| < 12 π and that (rn ) is a sequence of positive integers with rn = ∞.
This has been proved by Korevaar and Zeinstra [489]. See also Zeinstra [812].

artifact.category_tag: Exponential type of bounded analytic functions
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f(z)$ be analytic and bounded in the right half-plane $\{z\in\mathbb{C}:\Re z>0\}$. For a direction $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$ with $|\alpha|<\tfrac{1}{2}\pi$, define the exponential type of $f$ along the ray $z=re^{i\alpha}$ ($r>0$) by
$$\tau(\alpha)=\limsup_{r\to\infty}\frac{\log|f(re^{i\alpha})|}{r},$$
and, given a sequence $(r_n)$ of positive integers with $r_n\to\infty$, define the exponential type of $f$ along the discrete sequence $z_n=r_n e^{i\alpha}$ by
$$\tau^*(\alpha)=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log|f(r_n e^{i\alpha})|}{r_n}.$$
Prove that for every $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|<\tfrac{1}{2}\pi$ and every such sequence $(r_n)$ of positive integers tending to infinity, one has
$$\tau^*(\alpha)=\tau(\alpha).$$
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was resolved affirmatively by J. Korevaar and R. Zeinstra, who proved the stated equality of exponential types along integer sequences and along the full ray for bounded analytic functions on the right half-plane, for all $|\alpha|<\pi/2$. Further developments appear in subsequent work by Zeinstra.
